P1.evidence: Prior contact was referenced specifically enough to land — 'I saw, of course, also that you messaged Sophia about joining from the gym. So I love that energy.' The frame was looser than usual and never enumerated: 'we just go through everything... we have different approaches that we can have... I'll take you through it. If you like it, then we'll get you started.' No explicit 'does that work?', though the prospect volunteered 'Great. Let's talk.' Open question ran with his name attached.

P2.evidence: Age and weight both volunteered, never asked; height never established. Occupation never asked in a 55-minute call — 'I go to work' is the sum of what is known, on a prospect with a concierge doctor, a Tonal and three gym memberships. P2c is the consequential one: the rep did ask 'do you have any types of pains or something that we should know about?', the prospect said 'No' and then immediately disclosed high blood pressure, borderline diabetes, medication and a doctor's standing instruction — and the rep asked nothing further about any of it. Injuries and training history both covered well ('did you still work out outside, or was it just those two sessions?'). Diet asked and pushed ('What does your dinner usually look like?'). Sleep was volunteered ('I don't sleep well') and waved away with 'probably when you control the other things, your sleep will better work'.

P3.evidence: Target pinned at 185 lb and held there. 'What made it be for you that you're like, I need to do it now instead of waiting until you're 57 or 58?' ran the bridge properly. The future-pace ran — 'How would that be for you as a person?' — and when the prospect said he had stopped being able to imagine it, the rep pushed again, which produced the best material on the call: the son, the eight-minute mile, and 'how can I ask him to go work out and be an athlete if I'm a fat slob?' Legacy and identity fully reached. Only 'who else does that impact' was never actually asked, and there was no closing reflect-back.

P4.evidence: 'What stopped you from getting that before? You, of course, had it with the personal trainer before... what stopped you from doing that?' produced the complete picture: cost, packing a bag, travel time, and the fall-off after injury. The prospect named the gap himself and repeatedly — 'I need something else external to say, okay, how'd you do it today?' and 'I know the answers to the test, I'm just not going in'. That last line is P4f arriving on its own; the rep never asked it in scripted form.

P5.evidence: P5b ran, and ran well, because it was personalised to material the prospect had just given: 'are you willing to settle where that doesn't change? And also the people that are telling you like, ah, it's not going to work, you're going to do it for a week and then you're going to give up — are you willing to settle for them being right?' That is the best-adapted scripted move in the batch. But the two-year picture was never drawn — the prospect built his own ('in five years and two years and six months, will I be able to do five pushups?') — and neither 'why not?' nor the line in the sand ran.

P6.evidence: The blocker sweep ran cleanly before any number was mentioned — 'Is there anything that would stop you from committing 100% to it and getting to the outcome, which you've also seen other people do?' — answered 'I don't think so, no.' The rep then confirmed intent explicitly before presenting: 'it sounds like from what we've talked about that you feel like this is something you see yourself doing and you want to do it outside of the investment parts' — 'Yes.' A genuine yes was obtained before presenting, which is the point of the phase.

P11.evidence: No agreement reached; the call was cut short by the prospect's next commitment. Payment and onboarding were never reachable.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran twice, before and after the number. The rep held the price firm, which is right and is not consistently done elsewhere in this batch: 'No, he's not flexible on the six. Like, he has set that worth to himself.' Two capacity questions ran — 'would it be possible or is it just not possible to do it in one go?' and 'What would you be able to make possible?' — and the prospect said he would rather pay monthly, but no plan was ever defined. None of the six financial-picture questions ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no investments. The rep also acknowledged an unnamed cheaper alternative he could not get to in time, which leaves the prospect deciding overnight without the full option set.

'I'm 50-50 right now.' Three moves ran in substance: the worth question ('Do you feel like it is worth $6,000 to you?' — 'hundred percent. I do'), the blocker probe ('what are you mainly thinking about when it comes to thinking about it?'), and a decision reframe ('if you'd have said, ah, actually I don't know, it's not really worth it for me, then I would say don't even think about it — you've already made the decision'). He also pinned a hard callback and extracted a commitment to a yes or no. Missing: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', the identity close, and the final 'are you sure? Nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?'

'I want to just talk to my wife and add some numbers together' at 00:52:51. Not one OB move ran. No money-aside intent check on the spousal question, no 'what obstacles might come up when you talk to her', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger and less in pain' — which was unusually available here given a 22-year marriage, a shared 15-year-old and a documented blood-pressure and diabetes diagnosis. No deposit-with-refund fallback offered.

SCRIPT GAP — 'a cheaper alternative already worked for me', in its most concrete form in the corpus. His former kettlebell instructor charged over $100 a session, ran exactly the methodology being pitched ('Everything my trainer did is what you're talking about'), produced real results, and would cost roughly half. Objection C has no answer for this and the rep had none either; he asked an investment-versus-guessing question and the prospect talked himself partway out of it unaided.

SCRIPT GAP — 'remote should cost less than in person': 'I just thought that because it's not in person, I thought that it would be about half that.' There is no scripted framing for why asynchronous video coaching commands an in-person price. The rep's only move was to reframe the price as buying results rather than sessions, delivered once and not developed.

SCRIPT GAP, and the serious one — clinical screening. Hypertension, borderline diabetes, active medication, a treating physician with standing instructions, and post-surgical repair of a torn distal biceps tendon were all disclosed inside four minutes, and there is no scripted step anywhere in the playbook that requires the rep to stop and ask whether a clinician has cleared the prospect for loaded ballistic kettlebell work. The rep did not improvise one either.

notes: Strongest close mechanics in the batch — a real commitment check before presenting, the price held firm, and a hard callback with a yes-or-no commitment extracted. Two things undo it. The spousal objection landed and was completely ignored, which is the one that will decide this deal overnight. And the medical disclosure — hypertension, borderline diabetes, medication and recent tendon surgery — passed without a single follow-up question, which is a coaching issue only in the narrowest sense; it is a process defect that needs a mandatory step in the script.
